_comment: Help text for settings - displayed in settings modal UI

DEFAULT_USERNAME.long: The name used to identify you in chat messages. This appears in the message history and can be changed at any time without affecting past messages. Used in prompts via the {user_name} placeholder.

AVATARS_IN_CHAT.short: Show avatar images in chat messages
AVATARS_IN_CHAT.long: When enabled, user and assistant avatar images appear next to each message in the chat. Disable to hide avatars for a cleaner, text-focused interface. Changes take effect on page refresh.

DEFAULT_BACKGROUND.short: Global underlay scene shown when a chat has no scene of its own
DEFAULT_BACKGROUND.long: Name of a scene from the background library used as the app-wide default background. A chat with its own scene (set from the chat sidebar) overrides it, and the underlay image is only fetched when it is actually shown. Empty means no default background.

ICON_COLOR.short: Tint the gem logo and favicon for this Sapphire instance
ICON_COLOR.long: Hex color (e.g. #9b30ff) that recolors the gem logo in the nav rail and the browser tab favicon, so different Sapphire instances are distinguishable at a glance. A chat or persona trim color overrides it while that chat is active. Leave empty for the stock sapphire blue.

SOCKS_ENABLED.short: Route web requests through SOCKS proxy
SOCKS_ENABLED.long: When enabled, all web search and URL fetching will route through the specified SOCKS proxy server. Useful for privacy, accessing region-restricted content, or routing through Tor. Requires SOCKS_HOST and SOCKS_PORT to be configured.

SOCKS_HOST.short: SOCKS proxy server hostname or IP
SOCKS_HOST.long: Hostname or IP address of the SOCKS proxy server. For Tor, this is typically 127.0.0.1. Only used when SOCKS_ENABLED is true.

SOCKS_PORT.long: Port number for the SOCKS proxy server. Standard Tor SOCKS port is 9050. Default SOCKS5 port is 1080. Only used when SOCKS_ENABLED is true.

SOCKS_TIMEOUT.long: How long to wait for the SOCKS proxy to respond before timing out. Default is 10 seconds. Increase if your proxy is slow or on a high-latency connection.

BACKUPS_ENABLED.long: When enabled, the system will automatically create backups of the user/ directory on a schedule. Runs at BACKUPS_HOUR daily, weekly on Sundays, monthly on the 1st. Manual backups can be triggered from the UI.

BACKUPS_HOUR.short: Hour of day to run scheduled backups (0-23, local time)
BACKUPS_HOUR.long: The hour in local time when daily/weekly/monthly backups run. Default is 3 (3am). Set to any hour 0-23. Uses your system's local timezone.

BACKUPS_KEEP_DAILY.short: Number of daily backups to retain
BACKUPS_KEEP_DAILY.long: How many daily backup files to keep before rotating old ones. Oldest backups are deleted first when the limit is exceeded. Set to 0 to disable daily backups.

BACKUPS_KEEP_WEEKLY.short: Number of weekly backups to retain
BACKUPS_KEEP_WEEKLY.long: How many weekly backup files to keep. Weekly backups are created on Sundays. Oldest backups are deleted first when the limit is exceeded. Set to 0 to disable weekly backups.

BACKUPS_KEEP_MONTHLY.short: Number of monthly backups to retain
BACKUPS_KEEP_MONTHLY.long: How many monthly backup files to keep. Monthly backups are created on the 1st of each month. Oldest backups are deleted first when the limit is exceeded. Set to 0 to disable monthly backups.

BACKUPS_KEEP_MANUAL.short: Number of manual backups to retain
BACKUPS_KEEP_MANUAL.long: How many manual backup files to keep. Manual backups are triggered via the Backup Now button in the UI. Oldest backups are deleted first when the limit is exceeded.

BACKUPS_MAX_SIZE_WARN_MB.short: Warn when a backup grows past this size (MB)
BACKUPS_MAX_SIZE_WARN_MB.long: If the estimated backup size (after exclusions) exceeds this many megabytes, the Backup page shows a warning so you can exclude large folders. Soft warning only — it does not block backups. Set 0 to disable.

AUDIO_INPUT_DEVICE.long: Specific audio input device to use by index number. Set to null for automatic detection which tries preferred devices first (pipewire, pulse on Linux). Use the Audio tab test feature to find your device index. Useful when you have multiple microphones.

AUDIO_OUTPUT_DEVICE.long: Specific audio output device to use by index number. Set to null to use the system default output device. Most users should leave this as null unless routing audio to a specific device.

AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATES.short: Sample rates to try when configuring audio
AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATES.long: List of sample rates to try when initializing audio devices. The system tests rates in order until one works. 44100 and 48000 are standard for most devices. Add your device's native rate if you experience issues.

AUDIO_BLOCKSIZE_FALLBACKS.short: Buffer sizes to try when configuring audio
AUDIO_BLOCKSIZE_FALLBACKS.long: List of audio buffer sizes to try when initializing devices. Smaller buffers (512) reduce latency but may cause underruns on slow systems. Larger buffers (2048, 4096) are more stable but add latency. 1024 is a good default.

AUDIO_PREFERRED_DEVICES_LINUX.long: List of audio system names to prefer on Linux, tried in order. 'pipewire' is the modern standard, 'pulse' (PulseAudio) is widely compatible, 'default' uses ALSA directly. The system checks device names against these strings.

AUDIO_PREFERRED_DEVICES_WINDOWS.long: List of device name fragments to prefer on Windows, tried in order. 'default' uses the Windows default device. Other entries match against device names to prefer specific microphones or sound cards.

WAKE_WORD_ENABLED.long: When enabled, the system continuously listens for a wake word to trigger voice interaction. Uses OpenWakeWord with ONNX inference for cross-platform compatibility. Continuous audio monitoring may impact system resources on low-power devices.

CHUNK_SIZE.short: Audio buffer chunk size in samples
CHUNK_SIZE.long: Size of audio chunks for wake word detection. 1280 samples (80ms at 16kHz) is optimal for OpenWakeWord. Larger multiples of 1280 increase efficiency but add latency.

WAKEWORD_MODEL.long: The wake word model to use for detection. Built-in models include: 'alexa', 'hey_mycroft', 'hey_jarvis', 'hey_rhasspy', 'timer', and 'weather'. Custom models are auto-detected from user/wakeword/models/ - just drop .onnx or .tflite files there and they'll appear in the dropdown. Community models available at github.com/fwartner/home-assistant-wakewords-collection

WAKEWORD_THRESHOLD.long: Minimum confidence score required to trigger wake word detection. Lower values (0.3-0.4) are more sensitive but may cause false positives. Higher values (0.6-0.8) require clearer pronunciation but reduce false triggers. Default 0.5 is a good balance for most environments.

CONVERSATION_DTLN.long: Picks the conversation-mode mic path. None = headphone tier (no echo cancel) — clean on headphones, but on open speakers she hears herself. 256/512 = DTLN acoustic echo cancellation for open speakers (the duplex tier), so she doesn't barge-in on her own voice; 512 cancels harder than 256 at a little more CPU. Needs the DTLN onnx models in user/models/dtln/ — falls back to None if absent. Takes effect on the next conversation activation (toggle off/on).

CONVERSATION_START_WORD.short: Require a spoken start word, e.g. 'hey sapphire' (blank = off, respond to everything)
CONVERSATION_START_WORD.long: An STT-based start word (not a wakeword — no pause). When set, conversation mode only acts on utterances that BEGIN with this phrase, then strips it and answers the rest. Great for rejecting background TV/music that would otherwise trigger her. Comma-separate multiple phrases (e.g. 'hey sapphire, sapphire'). Fuzzy-matched, so 'hey staff fire' still works (see the fuzzy threshold). Blank = off.

CONVERSATION_START_WORD_FUZZY.short: How close a match the start word needs (0.0-1.0, default 0.7)
CONVERSATION_START_WORD_FUZZY.long: Similarity threshold for the start word, since STT mishears ('hey staff fire' for 'hey sapphire'). 1.0 = exact only; lower (0.6) is more forgiving but may let near-misses through. 0.7 is a good balance. Only used when a start word is set.

CONVERSATION_VAD_THRESHOLD.short: Speech confidence to count as you talking (0.0-1.0)
CONVERSATION_VAD_THRESHOLD.long: How confidently silero must classify audio as speech before conversation mode treats it as you talking. Raise it (0.6-0.7) to reject keyboard noise, background TV, and quiet sounds; lower it if it misses your soft speech. Default 0.5.

CONVERSATION_BARGE_HOLD_MS.short: Sustained speech (ms) before you interrupt her
CONVERSATION_BARGE_HOLD_MS.long: How long continuous speech must last during her reply before it counts as a barge-in and cuts her off. Raise it (150-250) so keyboard bursts or coughs don't interrupt her; lower it for snappier interrupts. Default 90ms.

CONVERSATION_MIN_SPEECH_MS.short: Shortest utterance (ms) that starts a turn
CONVERSATION_MIN_SPEECH_MS.long: Speech shorter than this is discarded as a blip, not sent to the LLM. Raise it (250-400) to reject clicks/taps; lower it to catch very short replies like 'yes'. Default 200ms.

CONVERSATION_ENDPOINT_SILENCE_MS.short: Pause (ms) before she decides you're done
CONVERSATION_ENDPOINT_SILENCE_MS.long: How long you must be silent after speaking before conversation mode sends your utterance to the LLM. Raise it (900-1200) if it cuts you off mid-thought; lower it for faster responses. Default 700ms.

WAKEWORD_FRAMEWORK.long: The inference backend for wake word detection. 'onnx' works on all platforms including Windows. 'tflite' is Linux-only but may be slightly faster on some ARM devices. Use 'onnx' unless you have a specific reason to use tflite.

WAKE_TONE_DURATION.long: How long the beep tone plays when wake word is detected. 0.15 seconds (150ms) is a quick, audible confirmation. Longer durations may feel sluggish.

WAKE_TONE_FREQUENCY.long: Pitch of the beep tone when wake word is detected. 880 Hz is a pleasant, attention-getting tone (A5 musical note). Higher frequencies are more piercing, lower are more subtle.

STT_PROVIDER.long: Select your STT engine. 'Disabled' turns off voice input. 'Local (Faster Whisper)' runs Whisper on your machine (free, requires RAM/VRAM). 'Fireworks Whisper' uses Fireworks AI cloud API (fast, requires API key, ~$0.01/min).

STT_FIREWORKS_API_KEY.short: Fireworks API key for cloud transcription
STT_FIREWORKS_API_KEY.long: Your Fireworks AI API key. Get one at fireworks.ai. If left empty, falls back to the FIREWORKS_API_KEY environment variable (shared with the LLM provider if you use Fireworks for chat too).

STT_FIREWORKS_MODEL.long: whisper-v3-turbo is faster and cheaper. whisper-v3 is higher quality but slower. For most voice input, turbo is more than good enough.

STT_LANGUAGE.long: ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish, 'fr' for French). Used by both local and remote Whisper providers.

STT_MODEL_SIZE.short: Whisper model size for transcription quality
STT_MODEL_SIZE.long: Larger models are more accurate but slower and use more RAM/VRAM. Options: tiny (~1GB RAM, fast but less accurate), base (~1GB RAM, good for testing), small (~2GB RAM, good balance), medium (~5GB RAM, high accuracy), large (~10GB RAM, best accuracy). The .en variants (base.en, small.en, etc.) are English-only and ~30% faster.

FASTER_WHISPER_CUDA_DEVICE.short: CUDA device index for GPU acceleration
FASTER_WHISPER_CUDA_DEVICE.long: Which NVIDIA GPU to use for Whisper inference (0 for first GPU, 1 for second, etc.). Only used when FASTER_WHISPER_DEVICE is set to 'cuda'. Check 'nvidia-smi' to see available GPUs and their indices.

FASTER_WHISPER_DEVICE.long: Which hardware to use for speech recognition. 'cpu' uses processor (slower but works everywhere). 'cuda' uses NVIDIA GPU (much faster, requires CUDA-capable GPU). 'auto' automatically detects best available option.

FASTER_WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE.long: Numerical precision for model weights. Lower precision is faster and uses less memory but may be slightly less accurate. Options: 'int8' (fastest, lowest memory, recommended for CPU), 'float16' (good for GPU), 'float32' (highest quality, slowest). int8 offers great speed with minimal accuracy loss.

FASTER_WHISPER_BEAM_SIZE.short: Beam search size for transcription quality
FASTER_WHISPER_BEAM_SIZE.long: Number of alternative hypotheses to consider during decoding. Higher values (5-7) improve accuracy but are much slower, especially on CPU. Lower values (1-3) are faster with minimal quality loss. Default 3 works well on both CPU and GPU. Increase to 5-7 if you have a GPU and want maximum accuracy.

FASTER_WHISPER_NUM_WORKERS.long: Number of CPU threads to use for transcription. Higher values speed up processing but use more CPU. Set to number of CPU cores for best performance. 8 is good for modern systems. Auto-detected if not specified.

FASTER_WHISPER_VAD_FILTER.long: When enabled, uses VAD to filter out non-speech audio before transcription. Improves accuracy by ignoring silence and background noise. Recommended to keep enabled for better results and faster processing.

STT_VAD_ENABLED.long: When enabled, voice activity detection uses Silero — a tiny ML model robust to background noise. Falls back to Classic VAD (amplitude thresholding) if Silero fails to load. When disabled, only Classic VAD runs.

STT_VAD_SPEECH_THRESHOLD.long: Silero's speech probability above which a chunk counts as speech. Default 0.5. Lower (0.3-0.4) if Silero misses your softer trailing words. Higher (0.6-0.7) if background noise is triggering false positives. Use the 'Test my voice' button below to see what your speech actually scores.

RECORDER_SILENCE_THRESHOLD.short: (Classic VAD only) Silence detection threshold level
RECORDER_SILENCE_THRESHOLD.long: Only active when Silero VAD is off or unavailable. Audio level below which sound is considered silence. Lower values (0.001-0.003) are more sensitive and stop recording sooner. Higher values require louder speech to be detected. 0.0025 works well in most environments.

RECORDER_SILENCE_DURATION.long: How long silence must last before stopping recording. 1.0 second allows natural pauses in speech without cutting off. Shorter values make interaction snappier but may cut sentences. Longer values are safer but less responsive.

RECORDER_NO_SPEECH_TIMEOUT.short: Abort if no speech detected within (seconds)
RECORDER_NO_SPEECH_TIMEOUT.long: Early abort timeout for accidental wakeword triggers. If no speech is detected within this time, recording stops immediately without waiting for RECORDER_MAX_SECONDS. Set to 3 seconds by default to quickly cancel false wakeword activations. Set higher if you need time to think before speaking.

RECORDER_SPEECH_DURATION.short: Minimum speech duration to consider speech
RECORDER_SPEECH_DURATION.long: How long speech must be detected before starting to record. 0.2 seconds prevents very short noise bursts from triggering transcribe. Too high may miss quick utterances.

RECORDER_BACKGROUND_PERCENTILE.long: Only active when Silero VAD is off or unavailable. Percentile of the rolling level history used as the background-noise estimate. The adaptive silence threshold is set just above this. Low values (10-30) for clean mics, higher (40-60) for noisy webcam mics.

RECORDER_NOISE_MULTIPLIER.long: Only active when Silero VAD is off or unavailable. How much above the background-noise estimate qualifies as speech. 1.1 means speech must be at least 110% of the background level. Raise (1.3-1.5) if background noise triggers false speech; lower (1.05) if soft speech is being missed.

RECORDER_LEVEL_HISTORY_SIZE.long: Only active when Silero VAD is off or unavailable. Number of recent audio chunks used to estimate the background-noise floor. 15 chunks ≈ 350ms of rolling history at default chunk size. Larger values make adaptation slower but more stable.

RECORDER_MAX_SECONDS.long: Safety limit on recording length to prevent infinite recording. 30 seconds allows long utterances while preventing runaway recordings. Increase for longer inputs, decrease to save resources.

RECORDER_BEEP_WAIT_TIME.long: How long to wait after playing the start beep before beginning recording. 0.15 seconds allows the beep to finish and prevents it from being recorded. Too short may capture beep tail.

TTS_PROVIDER.long: Which TTS engine to use for voice output. 'kokoro' runs locally (free, requires models). 'elevenlabs' uses the ElevenLabs cloud API (requires API key, per-character billing). 'none' disables TTS.

TTS_ENABLED.long: When enabled, AI responses will be spoken aloud using the configured TTS engine. Requires TTS server to be running on the specified endpoint. Disabling this will silence audio output but won't affect transcription or chat functionality.

TTS_ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.long: API key for ElevenLabs text-to-speech service. Get your key at elevenlabs.io. Also checks ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable as fallback.

TTS_ELEVENLABS_MODEL.long: Which ElevenLabs model to use. 'eleven_flash_v2_5' is cheapest and fastest (~75ms, 50% cheaper). 'eleven_multilingual_v2' is highest quality. 'eleven_turbo_v2_5' balances quality and speed.

TTS_ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID.long: The voice to use for ElevenLabs TTS. Select from your available voices or paste a voice ID directly. Leave empty to use the default voice.

KOKORO_DEVICE.long: Which hardware Kokoro uses for synthesis. 'cuda' uses NVIDIA GPU (much faster, adds ~1-2GB VRAM). 'cpu' uses processor (slower, frees VRAM for other models). Requires Sapphire restart to take effect.

KOKORO_CUDA_DEVICE.long: Which NVIDIA GPU index Kokoro uses. Leave empty for default (GPU 0). For multi-GPU setups where Whisper and Kokoro should use different GPUs to avoid CUDA-context races at startup. Example: FASTER_WHISPER_CUDA_DEVICE=0 + KOKORO_CUDA_DEVICE=1. Only meaningful when KOKORO_DEVICE=cuda.

TTS_SERVER_HOST.long: Network interface for the Kokoro TTS server to bind to. Use '0.0.0.0' to accept connections from any interface (required for remote access), or '127.0.0.1' for local-only. Requires restart.

TTS_SERVER_PORT.long: Port number for the Kokoro TTS server. Default is 5012. Must match TTS_PRIMARY_SERVER URL. Requires restart to take effect.

TTS_PRIMARY_SERVER.long: URL of the main text-to-speech server. Format: http://hostname:port. System will try this server first for all TTS requests. If it fails, falls back to TTS_FALLBACK_SERVER if configured.

TTS_FALLBACK_SERVER.long: Backup TTS server URL used if primary server is unavailable. Provides redundancy for uninterrupted service. Set to same value as primary if you don't have a backup server. Format: http://hostname:port.

TTS_FALLBACK_TIMEOUT.long: How long to wait for primary TTS server before switching to fallback. 0.2 seconds (200ms) provides quick failover. Too low may not give primary server enough time. Too high causes noticeable delays when primary is down.

TTS_STREAMING_ENABLED.short: Stream speech in sentence-sized chunks (Kokoro only)
TTS_STREAMING_ENABLED.long: When ON, Sapphire synthesizes and starts playing each sentence as soon as the LLM finishes it — speech starts ~1-2s after you press send instead of waiting for the whole reply. Falls back to whole-reply playback automatically for providers that don't support streaming (ElevenLabs, gTTS). Default OFF in 2.7.0 — opt-in while we shake out edge cases.

TTS_STREAMING_MIN_CHARS.short: Minimum chars before emitting a chunk
TTS_STREAMING_MIN_CHARS.long: Smallest chunk size the streamer will emit at a sentence boundary. Below this, the chunker waits and merges with the next sentence. Lower values feel snappier but produce choppy speech on short replies. Sensible range: 5-100. Default 15.

TTS_STREAMING_MAX_CHARS.long: Largest chunk size before the streamer force-splits on the last whitespace inside the window. Higher values produce smoother prose but delay first audio. Default 750 (sized for paragraph mode — fits a typical 3-5 sentence paragraph with headroom). If you switch split mode to 'sentence', lower this to 250-300 to keep the safety cap tight against single sentences. Sensible range: 50-2000.

TTS_STREAMING_SPLIT_MODE.short: Where to break the stream for TTS
TTS_STREAMING_SPLIT_MODE.long: How granular the stream chunks are. 'paragraph' (default) splits only on paragraph breaks (\n\n) — preserves prosodic flow across consecutive sentences in the same paragraph, sounds more natural. 'sentence' splits on every sentence end — lower latency to first audio, but flatter intonation since each sentence is synthesized in isolation. Max chunk length still applies as a safety cap in both modes.

TTS_STREAMING_PAUSE_PARAGRAPH_MS.long: Silence inserted after a paragraph-ending chunk before the next chunk plays. Default 80ms. Set higher (200-500ms) for more deliberate pacing between paragraphs; set 0 for gapless flow.

TTS_STREAMING_PAUSE_SENTENCE_MS.long: Silence inserted after a sentence-ending chunk in 'sentence' split mode. Default 0 (relies on Kokoro's natural breath silence). Set higher (50-150ms) if sentences feel run-on. Only meaningful when split mode is 'sentence'.

TTS_STREAMING_STAGE_PAUSE_STYLE.long: How to make Kokoro pause around stage direction (*X*) and parenthetical (X) content. Kokoro renders punctuation as natural prosodic pauses but doesn't pause for stars/parens alone. 'comma' (default) — gentle breath, feels conversational. 'period' — full sentence-end pause, more deliberate. 'ellipsis' — longer narrative pause, dramatic. 'none' — strip cleanly with no pause (legacy behavior). Also applies to **bold** since it's the same shape.

EMBEDDING_PROVIDER.long: Local runs Nomic on your CPU (requires onnxruntime + transformers). API sends text to a remote Nomic server. Disable to use text-only search.

EMBEDDING_API_KEY.long: Sent as Bearer token. Leave blank if your server has no auth.

LLM_MAX_HISTORY.short: Maximum conversation messages to send (0 = unlimited)
LLM_MAX_HISTORY.long: How many past messages to send to LLM. Single messages count, not assistant/user pairs. Truncates earlier messages when exceeded. Set to 0 to disable message-based trimming and rely only on CONTEXT_LIMIT for token-based trimming.

CONTEXT_LIMIT.short: Context window budget in tokens (0 = unlimited)
CONTEXT_LIMIT.long: Maximum tokens for the entire conversation context sent to the LLM. Sapphire trims older messages to stay under this limit, providing pseudo context-shifting for models that don't support it (like GLM). Set to 0 to disable token-based trimming. A safety buffer is applied automatically when enabled.

LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.short: Maximum wait time for LLM response (seconds)
LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.long: How long to wait for the language model to respond before timing out. 240 seconds (4 minutes) allows for very long responses with tool use. Shorter timeouts prevent hanging but may interrupt legitimate slow responses.

LLM_PRIMARY.long: JSON object with connection details for the main LLM server. Includes base_url (API endpoint), api_key (authentication), model (model name), timeout (connection timeout in seconds), and enabled (true/false). System tries primary first, falls back to LLM_FALLBACK if primary fails.

LLM_FALLBACK.long: Backup LLM server configuration used if primary is unavailable. Same structure as LLM_PRIMARY. Provides redundancy so conversations can continue even if one server is down. Can use different model or same model on different server.

GENERATION_DEFAULTS.long: JSON object with default generation settings: max_tokens (response length limit), temperature (randomness/creativity, 0-2), top_p (nucleus sampling, 0-1), presence_penalty (topic diversity, -2 to 2), frequency_penalty (repetition reduction, -2 to 2). These can be overridden per-request.

SPICE_DELIVERY.short: How the rotating spice reaches the AI
SPICE_DELIVERY.long: Ghost message (default): spice arrives in a per-turn app-context message labeled as coming from Sapphire's own app - prompt-cache friendly on cloud models, but the AI knows it's injected and may mention that. System prompt: spice is woven unattributed into the system prompt, so the AI wears it as its own inclination - feels most natural, but the prompt changes on every spice rotation, which re-tokenizes history on cache-billed cloud models (fine and free on local models).

FORCE_THINKING.short: Override the AI's initial think tags to force it to think a certain way
FORCE_THINKING.long: When enabled, prepends THINKING_PREFILL to every prompt to encourage the model to think a certain way. Useful for debugging or understanding decision-making. May make responses longer and slower. Most modern models don't need this.

THINKING_PREFILL.short: Text to prepend for thinking mode
THINKING_PREFILL.long: Opening text that triggers the model's chain-of-thought reasoning. Only used if FORCE_THINKING is enabled. Should start with a <think> tag or similar, then an INCOMPLETE sentence so the AI finishes it.

CLAUDE_THINKING_ENABLED.long: When enabled, Claude uses adaptive thinking — the model decides when and how deeply to reason per request, steered by the provider's Reasoning Effort setting. Shows summarized thinking in collapsible accordions. Only applies to Claude models, ignored by other providers.

IMAGE_UPLOAD_MAX_WIDTH.short: Max width for uploaded images (0 = disabled)
IMAGE_UPLOAD_MAX_WIDTH.long: Images wider than this are resized and compressed to JPEG 85% quality before storing in chat history. Reduces storage and speeds up LLM processing. Set to 0 to disable optimization and keep original images. Only applies if compression actually makes the image smaller.

MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS.short: how many total tool iterations can be called (these can be parallel)
MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS.long: How many iterations the AI can do tool calls for. Prevents runaway tool calling.

MAX_PARALLEL_TOOLS.long: How many tools the AI can call in a single tool iteration. Allows multiple tools at once. Multiple iterations per reply.

UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED.long: When enabled, Sapphire checks GitHub once a day for a newer release. Turn off to stop the only unprompted outbound call the core app makes. A toggle takes effect within a day; restart applies it immediately.

AI_TOOLSET_SWITCH_ENABLED.short: Let the AI switch its own toolset
AI_TOOLSET_SWITCH_ENABLED.long: Adds a switch_toolset tool so the AI can change its active toolset itself (e.g. coding tools, then self-edit tools). When disabled the tool is completely hidden from the AI. Off by default so a fresh install never surprises anyone.

AI_MODEL_SWITCH_ENABLED.short: Let the AI switch its own LLM
AI_MODEL_SWITCH_ENABLED.long: Adds a switch_model tool so the AI can switch between the models you list below. When disabled the tool is completely hidden from the AI. The model list doubles as scope control: only listed models are switchable.

AI_MODEL_SWITCH_ROSTER.short: Models the AI may switch between (top = least private)
AI_MODEL_SWITCH_ROSTER.long: Ordered list of providers the AI can switch between with switch_model. Order matters when the privacy ratchet is on: top is least private, bottom is most private.

AI_MODEL_SWITCH_RATCHET.short: Privacy ratchet: only allow switches DOWN the list
AI_MODEL_SWITCH_RATCHET.long: When enabled, the AI can only switch to models at the same position or lower in the list — privacy rolls downhill and never back up. The current chat's model is the floor.

TOOL_MAKER_VALIDATION.short: How strictly AI-created tools are validated
TOOL_MAKER_VALIDATION.long:
Controls what the AI is allowed to import/use when creating custom tools via tool_save.

• strict — Only allowlisted imports (json, re, datetime, math, requests, pathlib, etc.). Safest.
• moderate — Blocks dangerous operations (subprocess, shutil, eval, os.system) but allows most imports.
• trust — Syntax check only. Full Python access. Use if you trust the AI completely.

SESSION_TIMEOUT_DAYS.short: How long login sessions remain valid (days)
SESSION_TIMEOUT_DAYS.long: Number of days a login session cookie remains valid before requiring re-login. 30 days means users stay logged in for a month. Shorter values are more secure but less convenient. Set to 1 for daily re-authentication.

WEB_UI_HOST.long: Network interface for the web UI to bind to. Use '0.0.0.0' to accept connections from any interface (required for remote access), or '127.0.0.1' for local-only access. Requires restart.

WEB_UI_PORT.long: Port number for the web interface. Default is 8073. Access the UI at https://hostname:port after restart. Requires restart to take effect.

WEB_UI_SSL_ADHOC.long: When enabled, the server generates a self-signed SSL certificate for HTTPS. Browser will show security warning but connection is encrypted. Disable only if you're behind a reverse proxy that handles SSL. Requires restart.

PRIVATE_ALLOW_UNFLAGGED_TOOLS.short: Private chats: allow tools with no locality flag
PRIVATE_ALLOW_UNFLAGGED_TOOLS.long: Tools declare is_local in their schema; private chats refuse any tool without it (fail-closed — an unknown tool might send data to the cloud). Many plugins predate the flag, so private mode blocks them. Enable to treat UNFLAGGED tools as local on your box — CAUTION: unflagged includes tools that talk out (e.g. Discord, MCP-server tools), which this setting also unblocks. Tools that explicitly declare themselves non-local (web search, email, Telegram, etc.) stay blocked in private chats regardless. Default off.

VAULT_IDLE_MINUTES.short: Minutes of vault inactivity before auto-lock
VAULT_IDLE_MINUTES.long: The prompt vault locks itself after this many minutes without vault activity (chat turns wearing a vault prompt, vault edits, unlocks). Listing prompt names does not count as activity. Changes apply to a running timer immediately. Minimum 1 minute; default 30.

METRICS_ENABLED.long: Records per-LLM-call token usage in a local SQLite database (user/metrics/) for the dashboard's usage charts. Purely on-device either way — this only controls whether the local table is written at all.
